extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate students in algebraic geometry (Math 216 readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, characterizations, and key properties/exercises about locally free (invertible) sheaves, quasicoherent sheaves, and associated constructions (Picard group, tensor/symmetric/exterior algebras) on schemes. Includes criteria for recognizing quasicoherence, abelian-category properties, and behavior under localization/pushforward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picard group (invertible sheaves form an abelian group)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the invertible sheaves on X, up to isomorphism, form an abelian group under tensor product. This group is called the Picard group Pic X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13.1.G: the tensor product gives the group law; include identity (OX) and inverses (dual/inverse line bundle). Contextual remarks connect fractional ideals and the class group (see 13.1.M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality of Picard group under pullback
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a morphism of ringed spaces, and G is a locally free sheaf on Y, define the pulled-back locally free sheaf π^*G on X. Then Pic is a contravariant functor from ringed spaces to Ab (Pic Y → Pic X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13.1.H: construct π^*G and verify functoriality; later analytic and arithmetic analogues (13.1.L, 13.1.M) show compatibility in other categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscheme cut out by a section
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a section s of a locally free sheaf F on a scheme X, define the subscheme V(s) cut out by s = 0 and show the definition is independent of choices (trivializations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13.1.I: local description: on a trivializing open U the section corresponds to functions f1,... and take the scheme cut out by them; alternate hint avoids coordinates by applying Exercise 13.1.I. Check independence of trivialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hartogs extension for locally free sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: On a locally Noetherian normal scheme, locally free sheaves satisfy Hartogs's Lemma: sections defined away from a set of codimension at least 2 extend over that set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13.1.J: refers to Algebraic Hartogs's Lemma (Theorem 11.3.10). Use normality/Noetherian hypothesis; this is analogous to Hartogs phenomena for functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity criterion for rational sections of invertible sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: If s is a nonzero rational section of an invertible sheaf on a locally Noetherian normal scheme and s has no poles, then s is regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13.1.K: use Exercise 12.5.H; this is a check that poles control regularity of rational sections on normal Noetherian schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of quasicoherent sheaf (local M~ condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An OX-module F is quasicoherent if for every affine open Spec A ⊂ X there exists an A-module M with F|Spec A ≅ M~ (the sheaf associated to M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 13.2.2 and Theorem 13.2.1: it suffices to check on an affine open cover. Examples/exercises show some OX-modules are not quasicoherent (13.2.A) and some quasicoherent sheaves need not be locally free (13.2.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine-local checking (Affine Communication Lemma application)
rubrics_metrics.description: The property 'F|Spec A ≅ M~ for some A-module M' satisfies the hypotheses of the Affine Communication Lemma, so quasicoherence is local on affines and can be checked on a cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 13.2.1 and proof (13.2.3): construct global M as the kernel of the usual Čech-type difference map and check localization identities; exercises guide through the gluing argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished affine base characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Quasicoherent sheaves are completely determined by their modules of sections on affine open subsets together with restriction maps for distinguished inclusions (Spec A_f ↪ Spec A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 13.3.1 and Theorem 13.3.2: sheaves on the distinguished affine base recover the sheaf on the whole scheme; stalks and sections are recovered from compatible germs. Use this viewpoint to simplify constructions that otherwise require sheafification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization criterion for quasicoherence (α isomorphism)
rubrics_metrics.description: An OX-module F is quasicoherent iff for every distinguished inclusion Spec A_f ↪ Spec A the natural map α: Γ(Spec A, F)_f → Γ(Spec A_f, F) (the localization map) is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13.3.D (labeled VERY IMPORTANT): this is the practical check for quasicoherence; it expresses that restriction to distinguished opens is given by localization of modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of global sections on qcqs schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is quasicompact and quasiseparated and F is quasicoherent, then for f ∈ Γ(X, OX) the restriction map res_{X_f ⊂ X}: Γ(X, F) → Γ(X_f, F) identifies Γ(X_f, F) ≅ Γ(X, F)_f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important Exercise 13.3.E (cf. QCQS lemma 7.3.5): use a finite affine cover and exactness/localization arguments; helpful for computing sections on standard opens X_f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward preserves quasicoherence under qcqs morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a quasicompact quasiseparated morphism and F is quasicoherent on X, then π_* F is quasicoherent on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important Exercise 13.3.F: a corollary of the localization property and qcqs hypotheses; used repeatedly in geometric contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasicoherent sheaves form an abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: The category QCoh(X) of quasicoherent sheaves on a scheme X is an abelian category (closed under kernels, cokernels, finite sums and contains 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 13.4: reduce to checking conditions on affine opens via the characterization 13.3.3; explicit construction on affines defines kernels/cokernels as kernel/cokernel of module maps and verifies localization commutes to produce quasicoherent kernel/cokernel (13.4.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion to check exactness on affine covers
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence of quasicoherent sheaves is exact iff it is exact on every open in some affine cover; taking sections over an affine open Spec A is an exact functor from QCoh(X) to A-modules (left exactness caveat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13.4.A: use local nature of quasicoherence and exactness-checking on stalks; note warning that global sections are only left-exact in general and right-exactness holds on affines (anticipating vanishing of H^1 on affines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector bundles (locally free sheaves) do not form an abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: Locally free sheaves (vector bundles) with OX-module maps do not form an abelian category because kernels/cokernels of maps of locally free sheaves need not be locally free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 13.1.9 and warning 13.4.1: motivating example is multiplication by t on the trivial line bundle over R (or analogous algebraic examples), giving rank-jump phenomena; hence enlarge to quasicoherent sheaves to get abelian property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product of quasicoherent sheaves (affine description)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Spec A is affine and Γ(Spec A, F)=M and Γ(Spec A, G)=N then Γ(Spec A, F ⊗ G) ≅ (M ⊗_A N)~ and on distinguished opens the restriction is given by localization: Γ(Spec A, F ⊗ G)_f ≅ Γ(Spec A_f, F ⊗ G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13.5.C: use the distinguished affine base viewpoint so sheafification is automatic; sections on affines computed as localizations of module tensor products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor, symmetric, and exterior algebra sheaf constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: For a quasicoherent sheaf F one can define the sheaves T^n F, Sym^n F, and ∧^n F (and the graded algebras T•F, Sym•F, ∧•F) by doing the usual module constructions on each affine and verifying localization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13.5.D: if F is locally free of rank m these constructions are locally free and their ranks can be computed; treat algebras sheafwise (base ring omitted in notation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinant (top exterior power) and perfect pairing
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is locally free of rank n then det F := ∧^n F is the determinant line bundle; there is a natural perfect pairing ∧^r F × ∧^{n-r} F → ∧^n F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13.5.G: construct the wedge pairing locally and verify functoriality; useful in duality/Hodge theoretic contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration behavior of symmetric and exterior powers under short exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an exact sequence 0 → F' → F → F'' → 0 of (locally free) sheaves, for each r there is a natural filtration of Sym^r F (respectively ∧^r F) whose graded pieces are ⊕_p (Sym^p F' ⊗ Sym^{r-p} F'') (resp. ⊕_p (∧^p F' ⊗ ∧^{r-p} F'')).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 13.5.E and 13.5.F: construct filtrations locally in a trivializing affine and check independence of choices; in finite rank case det F = det F' ⊗ det F''.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection between fractional ideals and invertible sheaves; class group = Pic
rubrics_metrics.description: A fractional ideal a of the ring of integers O_K in a number field K yields an invertible sheaf; two fractional ideals differing by a principal ideal give the same invertible sheaf; the class group of O_K is isomorphic to Pic O_K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 13.1.M: applies to any Dedekind domain; shows arithmetic instances of Picard group and connects ideal-theoretic class group to geometric Picard group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical anti-patterns / counterexamples to watch
rubrics_metrics.description: Not every OX-module is quasicoherent (e.g., skyscraper sheaf at a non-generic point with group k(t) on Spec k[t]); not every quasicoherent sheaf is locally free; pushforward/quasi-coherence or Hom-quasi-coherence can fail without 'reasonable' hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 13.2.A, 13.2.B, remarks in 13.5: use provided pathological examples and Exercise 13.7.A (alluded) to see limits of claims; check hypotheses like qcqs or finite type when invoking preservation properties.
